note: Wholly invented. Tidepool is a fictional project and the people are fictional. See README.md.

records.statement: Tidepool stores tide readings as one row per station per hour rather than one row per reading.
records.context: From the Tidepool storage design note, section on table layout. The team had been arguing about row counts for a week.

records.statement: The hourly rollup cut Tidepool's row count from 4.2 billion to 71 million.
records.context: Measured after the storage rewrite described in the Tidepool storage design note.

records.statement: A Tidepool station uploads its readings over a cellular modem that is only powered on for six minutes an hour.
records.context: From the hardware section of the Tidepool field guide, explaining why uploads are batched.

records.statement: Tidepool's upload batching exists because of the modem duty cycle, not because the network is slow.
records.context: Conclusion drawn during the Tidepool latency review, correcting a common assumption on the team.

records.statement: Tidepool's prediction model is a harmonic fit over 37 tidal constituents.
records.context: From the Tidepool prediction service README, the section describing what the model actually computes.

records.statement: Adding constituents beyond 37 changed Tidepool's predicted heights by less than two centimetres.
records.context: Measured during the Tidepool prediction accuracy study, which is why the constituent count was frozen.

records.statement: Tidepool refuses a prediction request for any station with fewer than 29 days of readings.
records.context: From the Tidepool prediction service validation rules; 29 days is one full lunar month.

records.statement: The 29-day minimum for Tidepool predictions is a lunar month, not an arbitrary threshold.
records.context: Explained in the Tidepool prediction service README after three people in a row asked why 29.

records.statement: Tidepool serves cached predictions for 6 hours before recomputing them.
records.context: From the Tidepool caching policy, chosen so a cache entry never outlives a single tide cycle.

records.statement: Tidepool's cache hit rate in the first month of operation was 94 percent.
records.context: Measured from the Tidepool service metrics, cited in the first monthly operations review.

records.statement: Station 4417 reported a tide height of 900 metres for eleven consecutive readings in March.
records.context: From the Tidepool incident log for the sensor-fault investigation.

records.statement: Station 4417's impossible readings came from a pressure sensor reporting in the wrong unit after a firmware update.
records.context: Root cause from the Tidepool sensor-fault investigation, closed two days after the incident opened.

records.statement: Tidepool rejects any tide reading above 20 metres at ingestion rather than at query time.
records.context: Added to the Tidepool ingestion rules after the station 4417 incident.

records.statement: Tidepool's ingestion pipeline drops roughly 300 readings a day to the 20-metre ceiling.
records.context: Measured over the quarter after the ingestion rule was added, from the Tidepool operations review.

records.statement: Tidepool runs on three application servers behind a load balancer in a single region.
records.context: From the Tidepool deployment topology document, current as of the last operations review.

records.statement: A full Tidepool deployment takes 4 minutes and 20 seconds, almost all of it waiting for health checks.
records.context: Measured across twelve consecutive deployments, recorded in the Tidepool deployment topology document.

records.statement: Tidepool's deployment time is dominated by health-check backoff, so making the build faster would not help.
records.context: Concluded during the Tidepool latency review, which had started with a proposal to parallelise the build.

records.statement: Tidepool's API returns heights in centimetres and always has.
records.context: From the Tidepool API reference, restated after a client team assumed metres.

records.statement: Tidepool's API has never returned heights in metres; the changelog entry claiming a unit change in version 2 was wrong.
records.context: Correction issued after a client integration failed on the assumption that version 2 changed units.

records.statement: The Tidepool team is four people, of whom two work on the prediction service.
records.context: From the Tidepool project charter, current as of the last quarterly review.

records.statement: The Tidepool team reviews pull requests in pairs rather than singly.
records.context: A working agreement recorded in the Tidepool project charter, adopted after a bad merge.

records.statement: Tidepool's test suite takes 90 seconds and its integration suite takes 11 minutes.
records.context: Measured on the shared build machine, from the Tidepool contributor guide.

records.statement: Tidepool's integration suite runs nightly rather than on every pull request.
records.context: Decided in the Tidepool contributor guide because an 11-minute wait on every push was not worth the coverage.

records.statement: Tidepool keeps raw readings for 90 days and rollups forever.
records.context: From the Tidepool retention policy, which balances storage cost against reprocessing ability.

records.statement: Tidepool's 90-day raw retention is what makes a bad firmware rollout recoverable, because the rollups can be rebuilt.
records.context: Argued during the Tidepool retention policy review, using the station 4417 incident as the example.

records.statement: Tidepool's monthly infrastructure bill is 340 dollars, of which 210 is object storage.
records.context: From the Tidepool operations review, the cost breakdown section.

records.statement: Object storage dominates Tidepool's bill because raw readings are kept for 90 days, so retention is the cost lever.
records.context: Concluded in the Tidepool operations review when the team looked for something to cut.

records.statement: Tidepool station identifiers are four digits and are assigned by the national survey, not by Tidepool.
records.context: From the Tidepool field guide, in the section on registering a new station.

records.statement: Two Tidepool stations can share a location but never share an identifier.
records.context: From the Tidepool field guide, explaining the paired-sensor deployments at three harbours.

records.statement: The Tidepool field guide is the document a new station operator is given, and it covers siting, power and registration.
records.context: Index entry for the Tidepool documentation set.

records.statement: Tidepool's alerting pages a human only when a station has been silent for more than three hours.
records.context: From the Tidepool on-call runbook, chosen so a single missed upload window does not wake anyone.

records.statement: Tidepool's on-call rotation is weekly and covers two of the four team members.
records.context: From the Tidepool on-call runbook, current arrangement since the team grew to four.

records.statement: Tidepool's staging environment shares a database with the development environment.
records.context: From the Tidepool deployment topology document, noted as a known compromise.

records.statement: Tidepool's harmonic fit is recomputed for a station whenever it accumulates 90 new days of readings.
records.context: From the Tidepool prediction service README, the section on model refresh.

records.statement: Ines prefers meetings before eleven in the morning and declines anything after four.
records.context: A standing scheduling preference, stated when the shared calendar was set up.

records.statement: Ines is the person to ask about anything involving the national survey's station registry.
records.context: Noted after Ines handled three registry disputes in a row.

records.statement: I take my coffee as a single flat white and never after two in the afternoon.
records.context: A standing personal preference, recorded so it stops being asked.

records.statement: The flat's boiler was serviced in October and the certificate is in the kitchen drawer.
records.context: Household record, kept because the certificate is asked for annually.

records.statement: My passport expires in the March after next and needs six months' validity for most travel.
records.context: Travel planning note, written while booking a trip that nearly failed the validity rule.

records.statement: I would rather take an overnight train than an early flight for any journey under nine hours.
records.context: A standing travel preference, recorded after two bad five-in-the-morning airport runs.

records.statement: The bicycle's rear hub needs a 15-millimetre cone spanner, which the basic toolkit does not include.
records.context: Learned while attempting a repair with the wrong tools; written down to avoid repeating it.

records.statement: The sourdough starter doubles in four hours at 24 degrees and in nine at 18.
records.context: Measured across a summer and a winter, kept because the timing changes with the season.

records.statement: Dr Okonjo is the dentist and the practice only takes appointments by telephone.
records.context: Recorded after twenty minutes spent looking for an online booking form that does not exist.

records.statement: The building's recycling collection is on Tuesday mornings and glass is taken separately on the last Tuesday of the month.
records.context: Household schedule, taken from the notice in the building's entrance hall.

records.statement: I read technical papers on paper and everything else on a screen.
records.context: A standing personal preference, noticed after buying a second monitor that went unused.

records.statement: The recycling collection was never on Thursdays; the note that said so was copied from a neighbouring building.
records.context: Correction issued after two weeks of putting bins out on the wrong day.

records.statement: Tidepool runs on five application servers behind a load balancer across two regions.
records.context: From the Tidepool deployment topology document, updated after the second region was added.

records.statement: Tidepool's rollup job runs at ten past every hour and takes about ninety seconds.
records.context: From the Tidepool storage design note, the section on scheduling the rollup.

records.statement: Tidepool stores each station's metadata in a separate table from its readings.
records.context: From the Tidepool storage design note, the section on table layout.

records.statement: Tidepool's readings table is partitioned by month and indexed on station identifier.
records.context: From the Tidepool storage design note, describing the physical layout.

records.statement: A Tidepool rollup row is 48 bytes and a raw reading row is 121 bytes.
records.context: Measured from the Tidepool storage design note's sizing appendix.

records.statement: Tidepool's readings table grew by 2.1 gigabytes in its first quarter.
records.context: From the Tidepool operations review, the storage growth section.

records.statement: Tidepool's prediction service exposes one endpoint per station and one for a bounded region.
records.context: From the Tidepool API reference, the prediction endpoints section.

records.statement: Tidepool's harmonic solver converges in under a second for a station with a year of readings.
records.context: Measured during the Tidepool prediction accuracy study.

records.statement: Tidepool's prediction error against observed heights has a root mean square of 8 centimetres.
records.context: From the Tidepool prediction accuracy study, the headline result.

records.statement: Tidepool's predictions are published as hourly points rather than as a continuous curve.
records.context: From the Tidepool prediction service README, the output format section.

records.statement: Tidepool's prediction accuracy is limited by station siting rather than by the model.
records.context: Concluded in the Tidepool prediction accuracy study after comparing sheltered and exposed stations.

records.statement: Tidepool's cache is keyed on station identifier and the hour the prediction is for.
records.context: From the Tidepool caching policy, the key design section.

records.statement: Tidepool's cache holds about 40 megabytes in steady state.
records.context: Measured from the Tidepool service metrics.

records.statement: A Tidepool cache miss costs 180 milliseconds and a hit costs 4.
records.context: Measured from the Tidepool service metrics, quoted in the latency review.

records.statement: Tidepool's cache is in process memory and is lost on every deployment.
records.context: From the Tidepool caching policy, noted as an accepted cost.

records.statement: Tidepool's ingestion pipeline accepts readings up to 36 hours old and rejects anything older.
records.context: From the Tidepool ingestion rules, alongside the height ceiling.

records.statement: Tidepool's ingestion pipeline handles about 90 readings a second at peak.
records.context: Measured from the Tidepool service metrics.

records.statement: Tidepool's ingestion rejects are written to a dead-letter table rather than discarded.
records.context: From the Tidepool ingestion rules, the error handling section.

records.statement: Tidepool's load balancer health check asks for a prediction at a known station.
records.context: From the Tidepool deployment topology document, the health check section.

records.statement: Tidepool deploys on Tuesdays and Thursdays and never on a Friday.
records.context: A working agreement from the Tidepool contributor guide.

records.statement: Tidepool's rollback takes 40 seconds because it reuses the previous container image.
records.context: Measured during the Tidepool deployment review.

records.statement: Tidepool's API is versioned in the path and version 1 is still served.
records.context: From the Tidepool API reference, the versioning section.

records.statement: Tidepool's API returns timestamps in UTC with no offset field.
records.context: From the Tidepool API reference, the response format section.

records.statement: Tidepool's API rate limit is 60 requests a minute per key.
records.context: From the Tidepool API reference, the limits section.

records.statement: Tidepool's test suite runs against an in-memory database and the integration suite against a real one.
records.context: From the Tidepool contributor guide, the testing section.

records.statement: Tidepool's integration suite spends most of its time seeding 29 days of readings.
records.context: Measured while investigating the Tidepool integration suite's runtime.

records.statement: Tidepool's alerting also fires when the ingestion dead-letter rate exceeds one percent.
records.context: From the Tidepool on-call runbook, the alert list.

records.statement: Tidepool's on-call handover happens on Monday mornings at the stand-up.
records.context: From the Tidepool on-call runbook, the rotation section.

records.statement: Tidepool's incident log is kept in the same repository as the code.
records.context: From the Tidepool contributor guide, the documentation section.

records.statement: Tidepool has had four incidents since launch, of which two were sensor faults.
records.context: From the Tidepool operations review, the reliability section.

records.statement: Tidepool's retention policy was reviewed once and left unchanged.
records.context: From the Tidepool operations review, the retention section.

records.statement: Tidepool's object storage bill grew 12 percent last quarter.
records.context: From the Tidepool operations review, the cost breakdown section.

records.statement: Tidepool's compute bill is 90 dollars a month and has been flat.
records.context: From the Tidepool operations review, the cost breakdown section.

records.statement: A Tidepool station's power budget allows one upload window an hour in winter and two in summer.
records.context: From the Tidepool field guide, the power section.

records.statement: Tidepool stations are sited by the national survey and Tidepool has no say in it.
records.context: From the Tidepool field guide, the siting section.

records.statement: Tidepool has 212 registered stations of which 197 report regularly.
records.context: From the Tidepool operations review, the coverage section.
